No, I haven’t noticed any swelling in my legs, ankles, or feet. I also don’t wake up at night gasping for air.
Have you ever smoked, or do you have any history of exposure to dust, chemicals, or birds/pets at work or home?
Patient: Yes, I smoke about a pack of cigarettes daily and have for around 40 years. At home and work I don’t recall any major exposure to dust, chemicals, or birds/pets.

Patient: I don’t really have chest pain, tightness, or pressure—mainly it’s the shortness of breath when I’m active, with an occasional dry cough.

I haven’t noticed any unintentional weight loss. I don’t have any other symptoms beyond the progressively worse shortness of breath with activity and the occasional dry cough.

Patient: I don’t think I’ve had any wheezing—just the progressively worse shortness of breath with exertion and an occasional dry cough. I haven’t noticed it more at night or when I’m lying flat either.

I don’t have any significant past medical history—no known heart disease, lung disease, or high blood pressure. I’m previously healthy aside from this progressively worsening shortness of breath and occasional dry cough.

Patient: No, I haven’t coughed up blood. I also haven’t had significant changes in my symptoms other than the shortness of breath getting progressively worse with activity, along with the occasional dry cough.

Patient: I’m not taking any medications right now, including over-the-counter treatments. I’ve mostly just been dealing with the shortness of breath and the occasional dry cough on my own.

Patient: I do feel a bit more fatigued than usual, especially when I exert myself, but I haven’t felt weak or lightheaded otherwise.
